a child to take or have.text: Some hungers in horror reach for the cradle: a thing that wants a child to carry off, or an heir to carry its blood forward. In a remote Irish village [Claire guards baby Finn from the fairies of the Hallow|2015-the-hallow], where only light holds the changeling thieves at the forest's edge, and on a New England farm [baby Samuel vanishes while Thomasin is minding him|2015-the-witch]. In rural Indonesia a fertility cult once answered barren women's prayers, and [Rini counts the three days until little Ian turns seven|2017-satan-s-slaves]. The fear barely appears before 2000; almost every film that carries it came after.

a lover to possess.text: This is love with its hand closed tight, a monster or a person who has chosen one partner and will neither share nor release them. Count Orlok first fixes on [the portrait of Hutter's wife Ellen and her lovely neck|1922-nosferatu], then sails for Wisborg among coffins full of rats. Irena's jealousy [follows Alice along a night street and down to a basement pool|1942-cat-people], and in a house decorated like a dance hall [Lola crowns herself queen beside the boy who turned her down|2009-the-loved-ones], meaning to keep her date for good. The fear has held steady through every era, from silent film to now.

a way into life.text: Something waits on the far side of living and wants in, through a borrowed body, an opened door or a birth. In Georgetown [the words help me rise on Regan's stomach from within|1973-the-exorcist], written by whatever has moved into her. In Mahal a woman's singing draws Shankar through an empty palace, and she tells him that [by entering another woman's body she could live again|1949-mahal]. Teenagers in Adelaide make a party game of the invitation, until [Jade's little brother Riley takes his turn with the embalmed hand|2022-talk-to-me], in a fear whose films mostly date from 1980 onward.

cheating death and age.text: One of horror's oldest bargains is the one struck against time: to live forever, to stay young and lovely, or never to be harmed. In the village of Tualang Tiga [the shunned hunchback Si Bongkok is made handsome in the hidden realm of the bunian|1958-sumpah-orang-minyak], on the strength of an oath he cannot keep. In a decaying Hong Kong tower block [an old widow hires a black magician to raise her dead husband|2013-rigor-mortis], and the coin mask on the corpse's face must stay on. The same longing reaches from The Picture of Dorian Gray to The Substance.

claiming souls and victims.text: Some horrors come to collect: a soul is owed, a victim has been marked, a pact has fallen due, and whatever comes for it will not leave empty-handed. At Hill House [words scrawled on a wall call Eleanor home|1963-the-haunting]. Joy hangs a bagua mirror found on a bus at her front door for luck, but [the mirror takes a soul for every stroke of good fortune|2004-feng-shui], and in a remote cabin [the thing inside Mia needs five souls before the sky can rain blood|2013-evil-dead]. It has grown more common lately, with thirteen of its thirty-four films made since 2015.

corruption and damnation.text: The bleakest wish in horror is to spoil a soul: to tempt it, break its faith, or turn a loving hand toward murder. Stranded on a derelict ship near Neptune, [Captain Miller's crew begin to see the people they failed|1997-event-horizon]. In a Rhode Island farmhouse cursed by a witch who sacrificed her baby, [the spirit takes hold of Carolyn Perron|2013-the-conjuring], and in Paris [an unknown sender texts Maureen, urging her to wear her employer's forbidden dresses|2016-personal-shopper]. Nearly half of its fifteen films have arrived since 2015.

cruelty and destruction.text: Some horror wants nothing from its victims except their suffering, and there is a particular cold in that. In an Austrian lake house [two polite young men who came to borrow eggs bet that the family will not live until morning|1997-funny-games]. In Black Christmas the obscene calls [are coming from inside the sorority house|1974-black-christmas] as the sisters die one by one, and in a derelict bathroom [Adam and Lawrence wake chained, with hacksaws too weak for the chains|2004-saw]. More than half of these films are North American, and the fear has grown steadily since the 1980s.

fame and worship.text: Some monsters want an audience, to be adored, performed for, or spoken of by candlelight long after the night itself is over. In Kwaidan a snow spirit spares a young woodcutter on condition that he never speaks of what he saw, and [years later, by candlelight, he tells the story|1964-kwaidan]. In Mother! [a crowd of admirers pours in to worship the poet|2017-mother], tearing the country house apart around his pregnant wife. The same hunger to be watched runs through The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, Candyman and Late Night with the Devil.

feeding on the living.text: Hunger is the plainest motive in horror, and it has never gone out of style: something needs our blood, our flesh or the life in us. In a Stockholm suburb [Håkan kills to bring Eli blood|2008-let-the-right-one-in], while in a Japanese country house [a piano bites off fingers and a dead aunt devours unmarried girls|1977-house-hausu]. In Bali [Cathy's head tears free and flies off to an unborn baby|1981-mystics-in-bali], and at veterinary school [Justine's shamed appetite moves from raw chicken to her sister's severed finger|2016-raw]. It runs through about one film in five, in every era.

getting back the lost.text: Grief in horror rarely lies still. Here the monster is a mourner, reaching for a dead husband, a lost child or a vanished lover, or for someone who might stand in their place. In a decaying Hong Kong tower block thick with grief, [a sweet old widow pays to have her dead husband brought back|2013-rigor-mortis], though the coin mask on his face must never come off. On a remote Icelandic farm [María and Ingvar raise a lamb-headed child in place of the daughter they lost|2021-lamb], and the longing gathers most thickly in films made after 2000.

keeping crimes hidden.text: Some killing is a kind of housekeeping, done because a secret must stay buried and anyone who comes near it has to be silenced. At a Freiburg dance academy [Suzy Bannion arrives just as another girl flees its doors in terror|1977-suspiria], and learns that the school was founded by a woman said to be a witch. In Woodsboro, as Ghostface cuts down teenagers, [suspicion slides between Sidney's boyfriend, her friends and her absent father|1996-scream]. Continental Europe holds more of these films than North America does, and Blood and Black Lace, Deep Red and Eden Lake share the same cold motive.

keeping people forever.text: This is the possessive hand that holds a door shut: a house, a parent or a ghost that will not let anyone leave. In Ugetsu [Lady Wakasa draws the potter Genjūrō into marriage|1953-ugetsu], and only a priest's painted symbols can loosen her hold. Over supper at the Bates Motel [Norman talks about his ailing mother and the private traps people long to escape|1960-psycho], and at Hill House the doors close on their own until [words on a wall call Eleanor home|1963-the-haunting]. It has stayed close to the same strength in every era.

lust and indulgence.text: Here the hunger belongs to the body, appetite without limit and pleasure with no single beloved at its centre. In a Mexican barn [a tentacled creature from a crashed meteor gives Veronica a pleasure no man can match|2016-the-untamed], and she leads Alejandra to it. The devil's false bargain in Sumpah Orang Minyak turns the shunned painter into [an oily man who must rape twenty-one girls in seven days|1958-sumpah-orang-minyak], and in Raw [a hunger Justine is ashamed of runs from a stolen burger to raw chicken|2016-raw]. North America holds most of its films, from Re-Animator to X.

power over others.text: The wish to rule other people sits at the root of many horrors: obedience, followers, slaves, a weapon to aim. On a South Seas island [Dr. Moreau's beast-men scatter at the crack of his whip|1932-island-of-lost-souls] as they chant his Law in the jungle. In Francoist Spain [Captain Vidal tortures and kills to crush the Maquis|2006-pan-s-labyrinth], and in Los Angeles [Nancy casts her spell for power while the others ask for love and healing|1996-the-craft], until every spell comes back twisted. Most of its films come from North America.

punishing sin.text: This killer believes it answers to a higher law, and it moves through the world sorting the sinful from the rest. In Bad City [a young woman in a chador lets the men who prey on others take her home|2014-a-girl-walks-home-alone-at-night]. In a derelict bathroom [the Jigsaw Killer tests his victims' will to live|2004-saw], and in Santa Sangre [Concha orders Fénix to kill every woman he desires|1989-santa-sangre]. The fear is absent before 1960 and strongest in the 1960s and 70s, from The Cremator to Carrie.

release and unfinished business.text: Some ghosts are simply stuck, wanting a body found, a truth told, a stolen thing returned or a curse lifted, and they will haunt until someone listens. In Philadelphia [Malcolm urges Cole to learn what the ghosts need from him|1999-the-sixth-sense]. A glowing fog [carries the drowned crew of the Elizabeth Dane back to Antonio Bay|1980-the-fog] on the eve of its centennial, and in Dakar [the unpaid men who built the tower return at night inside the bodies of the living|2019-atlantics]. South Asian films carry it more often than most, a quarter of them in all.

revenge for a wrong.text: Revenge drives almost as many horrors as hunger does: a specific wrong, a wronged party, and a debt that must be paid in lives. In 1630s Moldavia [the witch Asa Vajda curses her brother's descendants as the spiked mask is hammered into her face|1960-black-sunday]. When the Thakur's grandson comes to Chandanghat in Bees Saal Baad, [a woman's voice sings to him from the swamp at night|1962-bees-saal-baad], and in Chanderi [townsfolk paint O Stree Kal Aana on their walls|2018-stree] to keep a murdered woman's spirit moving on. It is the commonest wish in South Asian horror, found in twelve of its sixteen films.

spreading and taking over.text: This is the fear of a world slowly turning into something else, one body, one carrier, one convert at a time. In Antarctica [MacReady trusts no one once the thing in the kennel has absorbed the dogs|1982-the-thing]. A whole Japanese town [is caught in the spiral|2000-uzumaki], its schoolchildren sprouting shells and climbing the walls, and on the express to Busan [every bite turns another passenger|2016-train-to-busan]. About one East Asian film in five carries it, twice the North American rate.

survival and self-defence.text: Sometimes the monster is only defending itself, its young or its patch of ground from people it takes for a threat. Over a horse ranch in Agua Dulce [animals vanish into a cloud that never moves|2022-nope], while a former child star nearby feeds it horses for a living. When classmates taunt her at a Swiss academy, [Jennifer summons a swarm of flies over the whole school|1985-phenomena], and on Jersey [Grace keeps her country house in darkness for children who cannot bear the light|2001-the-others]. The fear leans North American, and by share it was commonest before 1960.

taking someone's place.text: There is a particular dread in being replaced, in watching something step into your life and push you out of it. In Dead of Night [a ventriloquist's dummy named Hugo talks of leaving him for a rival|1945-dead-of-night]. Upstate, [wealthy white guests quietly bid on Chris's photograph|2017-get-out] before a spoon in a teacup drops him into the sunken place, and in the Irish forest [the Hallow steal babies and leave changelings behind|2015-the-hallow]. Fifteen of its twenty-six films are from 2015 or later, so this fear belongs above all to the present.

the sacrifice demanded.text: Some horrors run on ritual, and a ritual needs its victim, given up so that a harvest, a pact or a tradition can be completed. On her wedding night [Grace draws Hide-and-Seek from the Le Domas puzzle box|2019-ready-or-not], and her new in-laws take up weapons, sure they must sacrifice her before dawn. In the Tsitsikamma forest [Barend and his son leave offerings at an ancient tree|2021-gaia] while fungus-covered people stalk the house at night. The years since 2000 have given it sixteen of its twenty-two films.

to be loved and belong.text: The loneliest monsters only want company: a friend, a family, a mother's attention, someone who understands. Through a shared wall in Blackeberg [Oskar and Eli tap coded messages to each other|2008-let-the-right-one-in], while to keep Louis beside him [Lestat turns a dying plague orphan named Claudia|1994-interview-with-the-vampire], and the two men raise her as a daughter. At the orphanage his parents mean to reopen, [Simón draws his new friend Tomás as a boy in a sack mask|2007-the-orphanage]. The longing has grown with every era, and more than two in five of its films come from 2015 on.

to become something else.text: Here the wish turns inward, toward a new skin, a body made whole, a perfection beyond the human, or the chance to become human at all. Only seven films in the record carry it, five of them North American, and none was made before the 1980s. [Seth Brundle steps out of his telepod stronger, until bristly hairs sprout from his back|1986-the-fly], and in New York [Nina Sayers reaches for the dark Black Swan as scratch marks appear on her back|2010-black-swan]. In Glasgow [a woman who lures lonely men into a liquid abyss abandons her van in the Highland fog and tries to live|2013-under-the-skin].

wealth and ambition.text: Greed makes its own monsters, and sometimes the monster is whoever is counting the money. In Tumbbad [Vinayak lowers himself on a rope to steal gold coins from the starving god Hastar|2018-tumbbad], with a dough doll for bait. Ripley learns that [the company man Burke sent the colonists to the alien eggs for profit|1986-aliens], and in Ready or Not [the Le Domas games fortune came from a great-grandfather's deal with a mysterious Le Bail|2019-ready-or-not]. The wish for money, property or forbidden knowledge runs steadily through the whole century.
